findings.body: Interpolating `owner_id` directly into SQL allows quote characters and SQL syntax in that value to alter the query. Build a parameterized statement and pass the value through the cursor driver's bound-parameter API instead.
findings.failure_scenario: When an attacker supplies an owner_id such as `' OR '1'='1' --`, the generated WHERE clause is modified and can return order rows belonging to other customers.
findings.title: Prevent SQL injection by binding owner_id

findings.body: datetime.datetime.utcnow() is deprecated since Python 3.12 and produces a naive timestamp. Use an aware UTC timestamp instead.
findings.failure_scenario: When the created_at value is compared with a timezone-aware datetime, Python raises TypeError instead of completing the comparison.
findings.title: Use timezone-aware datetime.now()

findings.body: This is a behavioral data-loss change rather than a behavior-preserving refactor: starting at index 1 omits the first supplied entry from every ranked result.
findings.failure_scenario: When the highest-scoring invoice entry is first in the input list, it is excluded from the returned ranking and cannot be selected downstream.
findings.title: Include the first invoice entry when ranking

findings.anchor: def register_shipment_events(event_type: str, events: list[str] = []) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
findings.body: The documented per-type event result is not produced: the mutable default retains events across calls, including events of other types, then returns all of them under whichever type was passed most recently.
findings.failure_scenario: After a call for `created`, a later call for `delivered` returns the earlier `created` event under the `delivered` key, causing consumers to misclassify shipment events.
findings.title: Implement per-type event grouping

findings.anchor: """Return the newest queue identifier in constant time.
findings.body: The implementation sorts every record before selecting the newest one, so the docstring's constant-time guarantee is inaccurate.
findings.failure_scenario: For a large chronological record list, calling this helper performs an O(n log n) sort rather than the documented constant-time lookup, increasing request latency.
findings.suggestion: """Return the identifier with the lexicographically latest created_at value."""
findings.title: Correct the constant-time claim

findings.body: The new helper accepts `threshold` but ignores it and instead applies a fixed 5000 cutoff. This adds unexplained, incorrect business behavior in a refactor and makes callers unable to configure the documented review boundary.
findings.failure_scenario: A caller passes a threshold of 10000, but a row totaling 5001 is still flagged because the function compares against 5000 instead.
findings.title: Use the supplied review threshold

findings.body: Checking membership in a list scans all previously seen labels, making de-duplication quadratic as the number of distinct labels grows. A set preserves the existing first-seen output order when paired with the labels list.
findings.failure_scenario: When rows contains many distinct payment labels, each new label scans the accumulated list, turning processing into O(n²) work and delaying batch handling.
findings.suggestion:
seen: set[str] = set()
    labels: list[str] = []
    for row in rows:
        label = str(row.get("label", ""))
        if label in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(label)
        labels.append(label)
findings.title: Track seen labels with a set

findings.body: The viability count is identical for every carrier, but the nested zone/weight scan is repeated once per carrier. This changes the work from a single zone/weight scan plus dictionary construction into O(carriers × zones × weights).
findings.failure_scenario: When many carriers, zones, and weights are supplied, the function repeats the same route calculation for each carrier, causing avoidable CPU consumption and batch latency.
findings.title: Compute viable route counts once

findings.body: The docstring says records are already chronological and promises constant-time lookup, but sorting the whole collection adds an unnecessary O(n log n) operation and allocation. Return the final record directly, retaining the empty-input behavior.
findings.failure_scenario: When this helper receives a large chronological queue, each lookup sorts every record before returning the last ID, so a supposedly constant-time operation adds avoidable CPU time and memory use.
findings.title: Use the chronological input directly

findings.body: Interpolating `owner_id` directly into the SQL source lets quote characters alter the WHERE clause or append additional SQL. Bind the value through the cursor driver's parameter API instead of constructing the query with an f-string.

findings.title: Use parameter binding to prevent SQL injection

findings.anchor: def register_shipment_events(event_type: str, events: list[str] = []) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
findings.body: The default list is created once at function definition time, so calls that omit `events` append to and return the same list. Use a `None` default and create a new list inside the function to keep one caller's events from being exposed to another.
findings.failure_scenario: After one caller invokes `register_shipment_events("internal")`, a later caller invoking `register_shipment_events("external")` receives `"internal"` in its returned events despite not supplying it.
findings.title: Avoid a mutable default that shares shipment events

findings.failure_scenario: A request containing thousands of carriers, zones, and weights causes billions of loop iterations, monopolizing a worker and denying service to other requests.
findings.title: Bound or aggregate the routing cross-check

findings.body: The documented chronological-order precondition already identifies the newest item as the final list element, but this line copies and sorts the entire collection. Avoiding the sort prevents unnecessary CPU and memory use on large record collections.
findings.failure_scenario: When a caller supplies a large chronological record list, this function performs an O(n log n) sort and allocates a second list instead of returning the final record in O(1), increasing the risk of worker exhaustion.
findings.title: Do not sort a constant-time newest-record lookup

findings.body: The public `threshold` argument is unused while the comparison is hard-coded to 5000. This leaves a misleading, untestable configuration parameter and obscures the actual cutoff.
findings.failure_scenario: A caller passes `threshold=1000` to flag rows above 1000, but rows with totals from 1000 through 5000 are silently omitted because the helper always compares against 5000.
findings.title: Use the threshold parameter instead of a hidden constant
